dedupe_keys.name: shenzhen landfill slope failure of june 2008 back analysis of instability caused by high leachate levels

description: This case study analyses the slope failure of a landfill in Shenzhen, China, in June 2008 to understand how high water levels destabilise landfills. The authors, from Beihang University, the China Institute of Water Resources and Hydropower Research and Zhejiang University, used records from an integrated monitoring system of water level gauges, electronic total stations and inclinometers that followed the failure. The field data showed that the landslide was a deep slip along a weak interface in the composite liner at the base of the landfill, with the high water level as the main cause. The authors then ran numerical direct shear tests on the geosynthetic multilayer liner and centrifuge models of a simplified lining system to quantify how water levels affect stability. The article was published in 2016 and is free to read online under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is one landfill. Caveats: the monitoring data are shown in figures, not released, and the landfill's operating history is described only briefly. Simulation uses: a documented failure mechanism and parameters for landfill slope stability and service disruption scenarios after heavy rain. Related records: the Barmshour landfill slope study (case_study-barmshour-landfill-slope-stability-hybrid-neural-models) and the NSW extreme rainfall landfill scenario (case_study-nsw-epa-landfill-extreme-rainfall-odour-adaptation) address related risks.
